subject: math

entries: Speed is distance per hour: a bus at 60 km/h covers 60 km in one hour, 120 km in two hours and 180 km in three hours - the same 60 km landing every hour.
slots.label: Speed is distance per hour
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: 60 km/h for 2.5 hours: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km - 60 km in each full hour plus 30 km in the half hour.
slots.label: 60 km/h for 2.5 hours
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Watch out: speed is not distance: 60 km/h names a rate, not a total - after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, because half the time means half the distance.
slots.label: Watch out: speed is not distance
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The takeaway: distance = speed × time, and the formula flips either way - speed = distance ÷ time and time = distance ÷ speed.
slots.label: The takeaway
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The distance covered in one unit of time: a speed of 60 km/h means the bus covers 60 km in every hour.
slots.label: Speed
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An amount per unit of something else: speed is a rate, the distance travelled per hour.
slots.label: Rate
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How far something travels, found by multiplying speed by time: at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours the distance is 150 km.
slots.label: Distance
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How long a journey lasts: the time together with the speed decides the distance, so half an hour gives half the distance of a full hour.
slots.label: Time
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
